added_models.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

engagement.note: Genetic loss of Sglt2 in mice gave a 500-fold glucosuria; no drug and nobody had yet compared it with dosed humans.
engagement.quote: SGLT2 deletion resulted in a threefold increase in urine output and a 500-fold increase in glucosuria, as well as compensatory increases in feeding, drinking, and activity.
engagement.judgement: Opener at first use (Ly 2011 print January, Jurczak 2011 print March). A knockout carries no drug, so product_in_model false; the canagliflozin pharmacology review names no Sglt2-null mouse (grep: knockout, Sweet Pee, KO), so model_filed false.

engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of urinary glucose excretion: 500-fold glucosuria in Sglt2-null mice vs dose-dependent 24-h UGE rise in healthy men
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Sha 2011 has no epub date on Europe PMC (print July 2011) and its phase 1 study was not found on a registry; registry_date null.
engagement.note: The glucosuria the null mouse shows appeared dose-dependently in healthy men on canagliflozin, with the renal glucose threshold falling to about 60 mg/dl.
engagement.short: Null-mouse glucosuria seen in dosed men
engagement.quote: Dose dependently, canagliflozin decreased calculated 24-h mean RT(G) with maximal reduction to approximately 60 mg/dl, and increased mean 24-h UGE.
engagement.reason: Null-mouse glucosuria seen in dosed men
engagement.judgement: Paired: the knockout's glucosuria (Jurczak 2011, March) against the canagliflozin phase 1 UGE rise (Sha 2011, July); both public in 2011, so the year is 2011. Proximal readout (urinary glucose, the transporter's own substrate). Direction only: a null allele is not a dose.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the JASN full text was not retrievable from Europe PMC.
efficacy.note: Sweet Pee (Slc5a2 nonsense) mice kept better glycaemic control after STZ diabetes; no drug, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: After induction of diabetes, Sweet Pee mice had better overall glycemic control than wild-type control mice, but had a higher risk for infection and an increased mortality rate (70% in homozygous mutants versus 10% in controls at 20 weeks).
efficacy.judgement: Opener at first use. Ly 2011 compares the mutant with familial renal glucosuria patients, not with drug-treated patients, so this is not a stated model-vs-trial comparison.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction only: fasting hyperglycaemia prevented in db/db Sglt2-null mice vs HbA1c -0.77/-1.03% vs placebo at week 26 (CANTATA-M)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Jurczak 2011 and Stenlof 2013. registry_date is the CANTATA-M results posting (2013-06-03, checked by the tile's checker); the first-posted date is in patient_trials.

patient_trials.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).

The rate of the primary outcome was lower with canagliflozin than with placebo (occurring in 26.9 vs. 31.5 participants per 1000 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.97; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.02 for superiority).

efficacy.note: Sglt2 deletion prevented fasting hyperglycaemia in db/db mice; canagliflozin lowered HbA1c by 0.77-1.03% vs placebo at 26 weeks in CANTATA-M.
efficacy.short: Null-mouse glycaemia matched by HbA1c fall
efficacy.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).
efficacy.reason: Null-mouse glycaemia matched by HbA1c fall
efficacy.judgement: Paired, prospective: the 2011 genetic model preceded the 2013 primary-endpoint result. Scored direction only because a null allele sets no effect size for a drug. outcome_tested positive on CANVAS 2017 (status unchanged, listed in patient_trials as the tile does).

safety.note: The Sweet Pee authors predicted infection, malnutrition, volume contraction and mortality risks from SGLT2 inhibition before any phase 3 result.
safety.quote: Our model suggests that inhibiting SGLT2 may improve glucose control but may confer increased risks for infection, malnutrition, volume contraction, and mortality.
safety.judgement: Opener at first use; the prediction was stated in January 2011, two years before the canagliflozin label.

safety.magnitude_basis: direction of adverse-reaction rates vs placebo in the 2013 label: female genital mycotic infection 10.4/11.4% vs 3.2%, UTI 5.9/4.3% vs 4.0%, dose-dependent volume-depletion reactions; mortality not raised (pooled CV death HR 0.65, MACE HR 0.98 in the FDA summary review)
safety.confidence_note: Label and summary review read by grep; the label's adverse-reaction table pools four placebo-controlled 26-week trials, so registry_date is the CANTATA-M results posting (NCT01081834, 2013-06-03), one of the four. Mortality figure is the FDA summary review's nine-trial pooled CV analysis (CV death HR 0.65, 0.34-1.24).
safety.note: Infection and volume contraction appeared in the 2013 label (genital mycotic 10.4-11.4% vs 3.2%); the mutant's 70% mortality did not appear in patients.
safety.short: Infection and volume calls held, mortality not
safety.quote: INVOKANA increases the risk of genital mycotic infections.
safety.reason: Infection and volume calls held, mortality not
safety.judgement: Partial agreement scored same with source_calls_it partial, per the brief: two of the four predicted harms (infection, volume contraction) held in the label and three of the four if weight loss stands in for malnutrition; the mortality call did not (no excess in the pooled phase 2/3 CV analysis). A reviewer applying 'a predicted harm that never appeared is contra, magnitude opposite' to the mortality call alone would flip this track to contra; the mortality signal came from STZ-diabetic homozygous mutants, an insulin-deficient setting unlike unselected T2DM, which is why it is read as a partial match here. Scored at the 2013 label, before CANVAS.

added_models.model: DBA/2J male mouse, STZ-diabetic and control, 10-week canagliflozin in chow; microCT, bone strength and resorption markers

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the Bone full text (PMC4679447) was not retrievable from Europe PMC.
safety.note: A diabetic-bone-disease mouse dosed with canagliflozin for 10 weeks, run after the 2013 label already carried the fracture signal.
safety.quote: Canagliflozin treatment improved BG in DM mice by ~35%, but did not improve microarchitectural parameters.
safety.judgement: Opener at first use (epub 2015-07-23). Post-approval academic study, so model_filed false.

safety.magnitude_basis: direction of bone change: trabecular loss and a higher resorption marker in mice vs total-hip BMD -0.9/-1.2% (Bilezikian 2016) and fracture 18.7/17.6 vs 14.2 per 1000 patient-years in the 2013 label
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. registry_date is the results posting of NCT01106651 (the older-adults study carrying the DXA substudy), as used by the tile's 2015 rodent-tox entry; the patient side (2013 label, Bilezikian 2016) is already in the tile.
safety.note: Canagliflozin cost control mice trabecular bone and raised a resorption marker in diabetic mice: the human direction (BMD loss, fractures), reproduced after the fact.
safety.short: Mouse reproduces human bone loss, post hoc
safety.quote: Instead, in control mice, long-term exposure to SGLT2 inhibition was associated with adverse effects on the trabecular compartment of bone.
safety.reason: Mouse reproduces human bone loss, post hoc
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the 2013 label already reported fracture rates of 18.7/17.6 vs 14.2 per 1000 patient-years and upper-extremity fractures more common on canagliflozin, and the FDA reviews the BMD fall, before this mouse was run (epub 2015-07-23, before Bilezikian 2016 epub 2015-11-18). It reproduced the human direction where the SD-rat toxicology track (hyperostosis) did not, so retro, never same, on its own track. Direction only: the clearest effect was in non-diabetic control mice; diabetic mice showed only a resorption-marker rise. comparison_stated false because the abstract does not set the clinical data beside the mouse data.

added_models.model: Single-species allometric scaling of rat pharmacokinetics to predict human clearance, volume and bioavailability (ertugliflozin, PF-04971729)

dose.note: Rat PK was scaled to a human clearance, volume and bioavailability prediction to set the first-in-human dose of ertugliflozin.
dose.short: Rat allometry set the FIH dose
dose.quote: Single-species allometric scaling of rat pharmacokinetics of PF-04971729 was used to predict human clearance, distribution volume, and oral bioavailability.
dose.judgement: Opener at first use. model_filed is set from a grep of the combined 2017 ertugliflozin pharmacology review (NDA 209803/209805/209806) for 'allometr'.

dose.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed human clearance, volume and bioavailability; the abstract gives no numbers, so the fold-error is not recorded
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only; predicted and observed values not read. The first-in-human single-ascending-dose study is NCT00989079 (first posted 2009-10-02, healthy volunteers) with no results posted, so registry_date is null.
dose.note: First-in-human PK fell in the range the rat-scaled prediction gave for a low daily dose; 5 and 15 mg later succeeded in phase 3.
dose.short: FIH PK matched the rat-scaled prediction
dose.quote: First-in-human studies after oral administration indicated that the human pharmacokinetics/dose predictions for PF-04971729 were in the range that is likely to yield a favorable pharmacodynamic response.
dose.reason: FIH PK matched the rat-scaled prediction
dose.judgement: Dose: the model's exposure target was reached in healthy volunteers and the source itself states the comparison (comparison_stated true). Scored same under 'reached' with healthy-volunteer PK counting; the 2017 phase 3 approval later confirmed the dose was enough, which changes no status. No tolerability margin was stated, so margin_stated false. A reviewer may judge routine allometric scaling out of scope as a model system; it is kept because the brief asks for in-silico dose models compared with human PK, and this is the only member whose own dose prediction is published with its outcome.

considered_not_added: Ertugliflozin's own primary-pharmacology model (combined FDA pharmacology review 2017: 'Ertugliflozin administration in rats results in concentration-dependent glucosuria, which is directly related to the pharmacodynamic (PD) activity of SGLT2 inhibition'): rat glucosuria/plasma-glucose, the rodent system the draft already tracks as t2dm-rodent-diabetic; belongs on that track as a member entry, not a new system (the review names no ZDF/db/db/STZ model). Its SD-rat/CD-1-mouse/dog toxicology (hyperostosis at 288x/590x MRHD, adrenal pheochromocytoma in male rats) likewise belongs on sglt2-rodent-tox.

Tofogliflozin rodent efficacy (Suzuki 2012 JPET, doi 10.1124/jpet.112.191593; db/db mice and diabetic rats) and tofogliflozin rat PK/PD modelling (Yamaguchi 2013 JPET, PMID 23386251; AJP Endo 2013, PMID 23249697): the same diabetic-rodent system as t2dm-rodent-diabetic; no tofogliflozin preclinical-to-human prediction paper was found in three Europe PMC searches, so no in-silico track.
Vallon 2011 Sglt2 knockout (AJP Renal): the same Slc5a2-null mouse system as the slc5a2-null-mouse track added here; not cited separately.
Perry 2019 rat euglycaemic ketoacidosis retrodiction (Nat Commun, doi 10.1038/s41467-019-08466-w): run with dapagliflozin, not a member of this tile; does not score here.

Canagliflozin population PK/PD and dose-regimen models (e.g. de Winter 2017 BJCP): built on human trial data, not a preclinical or in-silico model that predicted a human result before it was known; not added.
Enavogliflozin: no rodent-efficacy or model-comparison source found beyond the checker's note (PK/tissue-distribution paper PMID 35745783); not searched further within budget.

Patient-derived cells or organoids, PDX co-clinical trials, ex-vivo drug sensitivity, human challenge models: none found for SGLT2 inhibitors in any search; the Genetics of Response to Canagliflozin study (CTS 2026, PMID 42144570) is patient pharmacogenetics with no model system and no model-vs-patient comparison.
UK Biobank SLC5A2 Mendelian randomization (Katzmann 2021) and familial renal glucosuria: already tracked by the draft as slc5a2-lof-frg.
